idea: Farmland and natural capital fund research for allocators
buyer: Family offices and allocators considering farmland funds
pain: Farmland funds are opaque and allocators cannot assess the underlying land
v1: An assessment of one farmland fund including land quality
channel: Husband's allocator network plus Italian land access
verdict: A genuinely rare capability, but allocation decisions are infrequent and the category is small.

why.distribution: Allocators via her husband's network, as introductions.
why.demand: Inferred; farmland allocations are still rare among the offices she can reach.
why.fmf: Fund analysis plus genuine land-level access; agricultural valuation is a specialism she lacks.
why.defensibility: Almost nobody assesses farmland funds at the land level - genuinely scarce.
why.tailwind: Natural capital allocation is growing from a small base.
why.ceiling: £14k x 14 assessments = £196k, requiring an allocator base that does not exist yet.

ceiling_arithmetic: £14k x 14 assessments = £196k less ~20% = £157k. Farmland allocation decisions among reachable family offices number a handful a year. Realistic: 2-3 = £22-34k net.
carries: A capability essentially nobody else has, in a growing asset class.
kills: Decision frequency. Farmland allocations are too rare among her reachable buyers.
test: Ask three family offices whether farmland is on their allocation agenda.
